predecessors.name: Brythons (Celtic Britons)
predecessors.text: the Brittonic lands of the Old North (Yr Hen Ogledd) around the Solway and Cumbria, inside Cliopatria's Brythons shape of 540-554

successors.name: Kingdom of Northumbria
successors.text: Northumbria's 647 shape, which grows by 12,000 km2 over 644-646 and takes Cumbria

successors.name: Kingdom of Strathclyde
successors.text: the part of Rheged north of Penrith (lat 54.66), which Strathclyde held at its greatest extent, 'to the River Eamont at Penrith' (Strathclyde page); a polygon because no name fits

ledger.x: c. 550: Rheged under Urien, the first king of the dynasty with dates on the page ('Urien Rheged, (c. 550 – 590)'). The page gives no founding year ('Yr Hen Ogledd (The Old North) c.500' is the Hen Ogledd era in the infobox, and Coel Hen is 'if he has some historicity'), so 550 bridges a silence. Cliopatria's Rheged…
638: Cliopatria's Rheged grows by 230 km2 on its northern edge.
646: Rheged is gone from the map, absorbed by Northumbria.

wars.name: Urien of Rheged's siege of Lindisfarne
wars.outcome: Urien 'penned the Anglo-Saxons in at Lindisfarne' with an alliance of Rhydderch Hen, Gwallog and Morgan; he 'was killed at the instigation of Morgan'.

certainty.note: The extent of Rheged is disputed on every side (Lancashire, Dumfries and Galloway, Catterick); no frontier is sharp.
